Amapiano [6260]

By: Busisiwe Gumede | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Amapiano was born in townships and now the sensational music genre taking off as an international phenomenon. Carte Blanche explores its anatomy and the townships from which it came.

Unique Selling Point:
In just a few years, the genre known as Amapiano has gone from a local South African trend to an international phenomenon, finding its way onto dance floors across the globe thanks to widely recognized artists like DBN Gogo, Focalistic, Major League DJz, and more. Debates about the genre’s exact origins are ongoing, but most artists generally agree that it was born in the townships of Johannesburg and Pretoria in the country’s Gauteng province around 2012. Much like its predecessors, amapiano was initially a byproduct of the manipulation of house tracks, through slowing them down to a lower BPM. Fast forward to 2022, amapiano is undoubtedly the biggest genre in the country. It’s been ruling the streaming charts and is highly popular on social media platforms. Who is behind South Africa's biggest music offering and how long will the hype last?


Summary:
Amapiano has unlocked many ways for the youth of South Africa to express themselves, providing opportunities for everyone from curators and compilers to dancers and club and event promoters. Today, there are hardly any venues or spots that don’t play ‘piano or cater to ‘piano lovers.

The prominence of amapiano has also directly improved and changed the lives of the artists who mostly come from middle-to-low-income backgrounds. Initially, they were paid with alcohol or exposure — the industry sidelined them. Today they are getting paid gigs, endorsements, better studio equipment, houses, designer clothes, expensive cars, and most importantly, are being recognised and appreciated for their talents and art. We hear from the industry's top amapiano producers and question whether the music will play on for years to come.

Press Release:


South Africa is well known for its flair for developing its own genres of music – from the catchy tunes of
kwaito to the heady jams of ‘gqom’- December anthems are almost always home grown. Now with its distinctive lock-drum hook, the irresistible sounds of amapiano are taking centre stage.
It’s a niche genre, with a massive following both locally and internationally, but here
at home, amapiano isn’t just a music sensation, it’s a lifestyle that’s changing lives. So, what’s behind the rise of the “Yanos”?
Carte Blanche heads into the booth.

Script:


NATSOUND - PARTY SCENE
- Can you feel it?
- Yeboooo!

VO – From make-shift studios in back rooms across South African townships, to an
international phenomenon…amapiano, is taking over the world!

PABI COOPER – DANCER/MUSICIAN - MVI_2919
09:56:58:47 - ... Amapiano is a life changer.

KUTLOANE “DA KRUK” NHLAPO – MVI_3054

08:52:42:08 - … Amapiano has got the best stories and stories that we will look at in the
next 10 to 20 years and say this was what defined a generation of South African kids.

LETHABO “FOCALISTIC” SEBETSO – AMAPIANO ARTIST - MVI_2937

11:02:15:16 - … I think for me amapiano is just a pure South African sound. It’s South
Africa’s gift to the world you know.

With the influence of jazz and slower house music instrumentals, over the last
decade, Amapiano has continued to evolve and include other distinctly South
African music genres.
Focalistic is now one of its biggest hitmakers.

LINK - MVI_2946 - We are in Alexandra township today, Focalistic is shooting his brand
new music video. As you can see he draws quite the crowd. From young children, old
people - just people love him. And I guess that speaks to his music , that it’s all about
bringing what he says she’s brought to bring. Lethabo – joy! -
NATSOUND – More from music video shoot

LETHABO “FOCALISTIC” SEBETSO – AMAPIANO ARTIST - MVI_2937

11:04:45:26 - I studied political science just like my dad. So when I finished my plan was,
... to get a job which is what my mom expected from me.
: Instead, Focalistic decided to pursue an unusual career - he became a rapper.
But it wasn’t until he mixed rapping with classic amapiano beats, that his music
really took off.

LINK – MV_2890 - Amapiano - which means “the pianos” in isiZulu - is rooted in multiple
music genres, including Kwaito and jazz. But there is something else that makes it sound
the way that it does. Enter what its producers call…the log-drum

NATSOUND - Kutloano linking in studio…

08:51:43:13 - ... It’s very instrumental. There is a sound called the lock-drum that defines
an Amapiano song.

CF suggestion: As far back as 2016, Kutloano “Da Kruk” Nhlapo helped introduce
amapiano to commercial radio stations. A game changer for this growing genre.
The origins of amapiano may be up for debate, but it’s the story of how
disenfranchised young South Africans are turning their lives around.

KUTLOANO “DA KRUK” NHLAPO – DJ

08:47:14:18 - ... it was very relatable for a lot of young South Africans from different
corners of South Africa.
To the untrained ear, amapiano is difficult to define.
Music Producer Tsholofelo Mokhine, better known as Felo Le Tee, explains how the
distinctive lock-drum is the key.

TSHOLOFELO “FELO LE TEE” MOKHINE – MUSIC PRODUCER

06:00:25:13 - The lock-drum is this one, and this is how it plays (clicks mouse and plays it)
Need two to three seconds more here to hear the lock - drum…
MASA – 06:01:13:33 - ... Now i know what it sounds like in isolation but let me hear what it
sounds like in a song.

(They both enjoy seconds of the track )

06:02:26:27 - ... I would say how you arrange your lock-drum and how you play with it and
all the other elements you add to it, that’s what makes your Amapiano unique
LINK - Amapiano is undoubtedly one of the biggest genres in the country. It continues to
rule the streaming charts and is very popular on social media platforms.
KUTLOANO “DA KRUK” NHLAPO – DJ

08:55:12:18 - Amapiano has fast tracked what young black South Africans can be,
especially marginalized young black South Africans, without having to deal with
gatekeepers, people that run the industry or big corporations. Like, they did it in thei own
terms you know.
VO - A former soccer referee, Paballo Mothapo’s career took a surprising turn during
lockdown.
VO – With just her cell phone and a lot of creativity, Mothapo created her alter ego
Pabi Cooper.
PABALLO “PABI COOPER” MOTHAPO – DANCER/MUSICIAN - MVI_2919

09:52:58:35 - ... I would wake up and wear three to four outfits, take pictures, and post one
dance video everyday.

VO - Her dance moves caught the attention of artists who begged to feature her in
their music videos.

VO – Now an accomplished musician in her own right, Pabi Cooper says the texture
of amapiano is in its culture – the fashion, the lingo, and the events – it's a lifestyle.
LINK – MVI-2952 - Seeping out of backroom studios in the townships, Amapiano is finding
its way onto dance floors across the globe. But it’s more than just a genre of music. It tells
the story of life, love and overcoming struggle.
LETHABO “FOCALISTIC” SEBETSO – AMAPIANO ARTIST - MVI_2937

11:07:47:17 - ... Amapiano has done more for the youth, and the township more than the
government.
With the growth of amapiano estimated to be worth millions of rands, it seems
there’s enough for everyone to get a sizable share.

LETHABO “FOCALISTIC” SEBETSO – AMAPIANO ARTIST - MVI_2937

11:07:57:27 - ... I’d probably still be unemployed ... Even the economy, amapiano is
carrying it on its back. And many families for real.

PABALLO “PABI COOPER” MOTHAPO – DANCER/MUSICIAN - MVI_2919

10:08:51:31- ... When I saw that i’m really going up there was when I bought an apartment
and I also bought my bus. 10:09:13:07 - I literally buy myself anything that I want.

NATSOUND - MASTERPIECE PERFORMING FOR US…

VO – As an I.T. student, former MC and hype man Thabang “Masterpiece YVK”
Kganakga understood a life of struggle.
Now as a leading amapiano musician, life has become a lot more comfortable.
THABANG “MASTERPIECE” KGANAKGA – MUSICIAN
06:21:25:31 - ... when I started getting gigs I was now able to ease off the pressure off my
parents to say: no, you don’t have to pay rent this month I’ll handle it.

But the question remains, as a niche genre, could amapiano translate with an
international audience?
PAUSE – fade to black, then do a montage of videos of international artists dancing to
amapiano.
VO – Diddy, Usher and Swizz Beats – just a few international artists who've been
bitten by the amapiano bug.
KUTLOANO “DA KRUK” NHLAPO – DJ

08:57:35:19 - ... This music has got the quality to be on the same playlist 08:57:51:40 or
similar playlist as like a Beyoncé and Jay-Z.

VO – The United Kingdom is probably the biggest importer of amapiano, having
launched the genre-inspired festival Amafest in 2021.
PABALLO “PABI COOPER” MOTHAPO – DANCER/MUSICIAN - MVI_2919

10:08:04:36 - they just like “Pabi! Pabi! Pabi!” It’s crazy because I’m just like “oh, you know
me”. All they way in London.

VO – Despite amapiano exceeding the wildest expectations of industry players, they
feel there's still a lot more for the taking.

KUTLOANO “DA KRUK” NHLAPO – DJ

08:57:01:23 - ... I think with any growing and big industry there’s a time where an industry
needs to formalise. 09:02:24:44 - I think amapiano needs more people in tailored suits to
represent it in rooms that artists wouldn’t be able to make it into.

LETHABO “FOCALISTIC” SEBETSO – AMAPIANO ARTIST - MVI_2937

11:19:22:03 - ... I think that’s the next step for amapiano, for us it’s professionalizing,
making sure that, I don’t feel like I need to be everywhere because my team is everywhere.

VO – If the past decade of amapiano is anything to go by, then the years to come
and beyond promise to deliver more hits, more dance challenges and most
importantly, more inspiring stories of how the genre will continue to change lives for
the better.
